items.prompt: Don't call me at eight tonight. I ___ dinner with my parents.
items.why: At eight the dinner is in progress: will be + -ing.

items.prompt: By eight o'clock tonight I ___ dinner, so call me after that.
items.why: By eight means finished before then: will have + past participle.

items.prompt: This time next week we ___ on a beach in Greece.
items.why: This time next week points to something in progress: will be + -ing.

items.prompt: By the end of the month she ___ here for ten years.
items.why: For ten years counts the time up to a future point: will have worked or will have been working.

items.prompt: ___ you be using the car this evening? I need to go to the shops.
items.why: The polite question about plans is Will you be + -ing?

items.prompt: I can't meet you at three. I ___ in a meeting.
items.why: At three the meeting is in progress: will be + -ing.

items.prompt: Hurry up! The film ___ by the time we get there.
items.why: By the time we get there the start is already over: will have + past participle.

items.prompt: By the time she ___, we will have left.
items.why: After by the time use the present simple, not will.

items.prompt: By Friday, I will have ___ the report. (write)
items.why: After will have use the past participle: written.

items.prompt: In June they will have ___ married for twenty years. (be)
items.why: will have + past participle of be: been.

items.prompt: By then she will have been ___ for nine hours. (drive)
items.why: will have been + -ing shows how long: driving.

items.prompt: He will have ___ before we arrive. (leave)
items.why: After will have use the past participle: left.

items.prompt: This time tomorrow I will be ___ in the sea. (swim)
items.why: will be + -ing: in progress at that time.

items.prompt: By next summer we will have ___ the kitchen. (build)
items.why: Build is irregular: the past participle is built.

items.prompt: At nine tonight she will be ___ her exam. (sit)
items.why: will be + -ing: the exam is in progress at nine.
